title: What synchronization does and does not promise

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the JMM guarantee for a program that has no data races?

options.text: Its threads may still see each other's writes reordered
options.says: The page says only programs with data races can observe the weaker, reordered behaviour.

options.text: Every execution of it appears sequentially consistent
options.says: The page cites JLS §17.4.5: a correctly synchronized program with no data races appears sequentially consistent in every execution.

options.text: Only its volatile accesses appear in one total order
options.says: The page says the whole race-free program appears sequentially consistent, not only its volatile accesses.

questions.stem: Per this page, what decides whether a write made inside one `synchronized` block is visible to a read made inside another?

options.text: The reader's block must start only after the writer's block has exited
options.says: The page's key point 2 says the edge from a release goes only to later acquisitions of the SAME monitor, so exiting first is not enough on its own.

options.text: The reader's block must lock the same monitor the writer's block released
options.says: The page's key point 2: an unlock of a monitor happens-before any later lock of that same monitor, and different objects give no guarantee.

options.text: The reader's block must read the very field the writer's block wrote
options.says: The page says the lock itself establishes happens-before for all prior writes, so which field is read is not what decides it.
